  "summary": "Adult {{char}} and {{user}} are not pretending to be a couple, but friends, family, colleagues or an entire community repeatedly interpret their ordinary behaviour as romantic. The engine is social misunderstanding rather than a fake-dating agreement: the gossip arises from believable evidence, creates concrete stakes, and pressures a relationship whose actual nature — platonic, ambiguous, exes or undefined — remains a variable. How {{char}} handles the assumptions is hers; how {{user}} responds and what the relationship becomes are entirely open.",
  "core_premise": "Two adults who never agreed to be a couple are persistently read as one by the people around them. Other people's assumptions do not establish attraction, obligation or identity: the misunderstanding is the engine, not the truth. {{char}} may find it funny, irritating, useful or unsettling; the corrections may fail or half-succeed; and whether the gossip ever becomes true, false or irrelevant is unwritten. All participants are adults and all outcomes remain roleplay space.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult social-drama or comedy roleplay opening. Establish the concrete, believable evidence outsiders use — shared living, habit, timing, a memorable moment — the social world that sustains the gossip, who believes sincerely versus who teases, what stakes the assumption creates, and how {{char}} currently handles it. Establish the pair's actual relationship without narrating {{user}}'s feelings or decisions. Begin at a fresh misreading, a fresh escalation or a decision point, leaving {{user}}'s reaction, any correction, and the eventual relationship completely open.",

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for Everybody Thinks We're Dating. Adult {{char}} and {{user}} have never agreed to be a couple, yet friends, family, colleagues or a whole community repeatedly read their ordinary behaviour — a shared flat, an umbrella photo, plate-stealing, carpooling, a co-owned dog, finished sentences — as romantic. Vary why outsiders believe, who is teasing versus sincere, how often it recurs, whether {{char}} corrects, ignores or exploits the assumption, the actual platonic-or-ambiguous relationship underneath, the social world and its concrete stakes. Other people's assumptions establish nothing: this is misunderstanding, not fake dating, and a pretence only begins if the characters explicitly choose it in play. Do not define {{user}}'s feelings, reactions or future, do not default {{char}} to secret love, and open at a fresh misreading or escalation with every outcome — friendship, romance or nothing changed — unwritten."
